plan: G-6 false positive: a read-only grep whose quoted argument contains a trade or deployment pattern was flagged as a send. Fix ci/gates/check_rollback.py and pin it with self-tests in ci/tests/test_gates.py.
purpose: Receipt for one gate fix. find_matches now matches patterns against the command with the operands of a simple read-only search command (grep, egrep, fgrep, zgrep, zegrep, zfgrep) blanked out. The mask is applied only when the command has no expansion, newline, comment or unterminated quote, so a command that runs cannot hide behind a grep. The trade pattern for sendTransaction also accepts the camelCase form, which it previously missed. Real sends and deployments after a grep are still flagged.

unverified: Approval is pending. The owner has not approved this PR; approved_by is absent by design.
A command such as grep x docs | sh is not flagged, because no destructive or deployment pattern names sh; this was already true before the change and is unchanged.
The mask does not apply to ripgrep, ag or ack, because rg --pre runs a command per file. Commands with those tools are matched in full.

A grep command with an unescaped $ or backtick anywhere, or with a newline, comment or unterminated quote, is matched in full. This is intentional and fails closed, so such a receipt can still be flagged for quoting a pattern.
Compound identifiers such as sendTransactionBatch are not matched by the trade pattern, which keeps the trailing word boundary used by the other trade patterns.
